purpose: Test whether sampling the outer body silhouette, without changing NN predictions or distance fields, removes enclosed-hole sensitivity in automatic cropping.
change: For lower-edge sampling only, flood the binary mask background from the image border with eight-neighbour connectivity, treating remaining enclosed zeros as inside. Preserve original foreground selection, RGB, colour fields, paper probabilities, distance fields, thresholds, orientation budget and template targets.
checkpointSelection: Two saved final checkpoints; no retraining, checkpoint tuning or per-photo model selection.
sequence: Verify existing default crop decisions against all cached detections for both models, without repeating template fits.
Replay every photo with outer sampling enabled and the same production-control reuse. Fresh-fit every selected neural crop.
Run independent editable conversion, geometry/paper and original image/feature checks; inspect all changed crops and new fits.
promotion: Require original checked editable designs retained for each model and inspect new crop decisions. Restoring a previously rejected crop alone is not a new reconstruction success. No production or NN release without broader evaluation and ONNX/browser/user-flow QA.
scope: Two comparisons on the same repeatedly inspected 32-photo development cohort. Native inference cached, no fresh generalization claim. The 10-second setting is the existing solver search budget, not an end-to-end wall-clock guarantee.
